mental_model: EnableStrideAlign turns alignment intent into real memory layout. Earlier passes leave small notes saying 'the row stride of this dimension must be a multiple of N bytes'; this pass gathers those notes, unions conflicting demands, and re-allocates each buffer with its rows padded to the required unit, rewiring every user through a strided view that preserves the original logical shape. Buffers that already satisfy every demand keep their exact shape, and on non-regbase targets each device function is stamped to certify that the whole function is aligned.
need: Ascend UB vector/DMA hardware requires row strides to be hardware-aligned, but the passes that know which accesses need alignment do not own buffer shapes, and the allocation sites do not know access requirements. A single late consumer is needed so marking stays cheap and local while the actual shape decision happens once, globally, on the final post-bufferization memref IR.
responsibility: Consume stride-align marks; normalize and union the demands; propagate them until every demand reaches the allocation owning the memory; re-allocate that allocation with padded dimensions; keep buffer-size annotations and function metadata coherent; and fail loudly (or fall back to explicit copies) when a demand cannot be propagated or the exchange does not converge.
observable_outcome: After the pass, every buffer that carried a real demand is re-allocated with its pad dimension grown to the alignment unit (plus a trailing unit dim when the pad dim is not last), and all users read/write through strided subviews keeping the original logical shape; stride-align marks and attrs are gone; buffer_size_in_byte marks were rescaled upward; on membase each device function carries hivm.storage_aligned, on RegBase it does not. Buffers already aligned are untouched. Failures surface as pass failures or explicit hivm.hir.copy fallbacks, never as silent wrong layouts.

audience_contract.who: Compiler engineers working on the AscendNPU-IR regbase/membase pipelines who have never read the AlignBuffer directory
audience_contract.assumed_knowledge: MLIR pass pipelines, memref layouts and subview semantics, bufferization producing memref IR, Ascend UB/GM memory spaces

upstream.role: mark producer (gated by enable-hivm-auto-storage-align, default true)
upstream.interaction: Annotates memref operands of hivm ops with annotation.mark {hivm.stride_align_dims, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte} where the value is the hardware align bytes of the memory space; these marks are the raw input this pass consumes
Marks roots of loads flowing to VF vloads to be spared from stride padding; the protection decision is made on the marking side, before this pass ever sees a demand
Runs unconditionally between the marking passes and this pass, folding reshape-of-alloc pairs so fewer view ops separate a mark from its allocation when the fixed-point exchange starts
Aligns alloc sizes for special hivm ops before any marking or enabling happens

downstream.role: next decompose phase in the same pipeline
downstream.interaction: Runs immediately after alignStoragePipeline; the comment 'Decompose {vconcat} after stride alignment' shows the pipeline deliberately splits decompose work around this pass

downstream.role: layout and size consumers later in the pipeline
downstream.interaction: See the final shapes and strided layouts this pass established: InferHIVMDataLayout converts copy ops to nd2nz on top of the padded row strides, and the buffer-size passes constantize sizes after alignment arithmetic has been materialized

The pass stamps this attr on device functions on membase targets only; the attr declares 'all operations in this function are aligned'. No reader of the attr was found inside this repository at HEAD — downstream consumption (if any) lives outside the analyzed tree

When an aligned allocation flows into a call, the callee signature and entry block arg types are retyped to the strided layout, so already-visited callees are updated too — the reason the pass walks functions sequentially at ModuleOp scope

triggers.interaction: Runs unconditionally at the end of alignStoragePipeline (only the two marking passes inside that pipeline are gated by enable-hivm-auto-storage-align), on post-bufferization memref IR

inputs.name: stride-align marks
inputs.form: annotation.mark ops carrying hivm.stride_align_dims + hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte (DenseI32ArrayAttr pairs, e.g. dims [0] / 32 bytes) on ranked UB memref values — alloc results, view results, loop iter args, scf.if/for results; produced by MarkStrideAlign
inputs.description: The demands: 'the stride of this dim must be a multiple of this many bytes'

inputs.name: stride-align attrs already on alloc ops
inputs.form: the same two attrs set directly on memref.alloc/alloca ops (by up-propagation inside this run, or re-marked by AddAlignAnnotationMarkForAlloc)
inputs.description: Demands that already reached an allocation

inputs.name: post-bufferization module IR
inputs.form: ModuleOp of device funcs whose UB buffers are memref.alloc/alloca with view ops (subview/collapse/expand/reshape), scf.for/if control flow, scope ops, and func.call into outlined VF callees
inputs.description: The world the demands live in; GM operands and tensor IR are out of scope

outputs.name: padded allocations behind strided views
outputs.form: memref.alloc with the pad dim grown to the alignment unit (memref<2x15xf16,ub> → memref<2x16x1xf16,ub>) plus memref.subview with the original logical shape and padded row stride (strided<[16,1]>); dynamic pad dims get arith addi/remsi/subi ceil-align arithmetic
outputs.description: The realized alignment: logical shape unchanged, physical rows padded

outputs.name: retyped users
outputs.form: scf.for iter-args/results, scf.if results, scope results and func.call signatures rewritten to the strided types, or — where retyping is impossible — fresh empty buffers + hivm.hir.copy
outputs.description: Every consumer now sees a consistent layout

outputs.name: cleaned metadata
outputs.form: stride-align marks and alloc attrs removed after consumption; buffer_size_in_byte marks rescaled by the static-volume ratio (ceil division); membase-only hivm.storage_aligned unit attr stamped on device funcs
outputs.description: No stale demands, no stale sizes, explicit certification on membase

mechanism.summary: A per-function, multi-phase greedy rewrite: normalize marks, exchange demands to a fixed point (down to leaves, union across operands, up to allocations), then re-allocate padded buffers and rewire the function through strided views, with a copy-based fallback for demands that cannot be typed through.

stages.name: Normalize marks
stages.what: For each mark carrying stride-align attrs, validate dims/bytes are present and equal length (emitError otherwise) and sort the (dim, byte) pairs ascending; a no-op for already-sorted marks

stages.name: Push demands up to root allocations
stages.what: Walk every mark; dispatch on the marked value's defining op (cast/subview/view/collapse/expand/reshape/bitcast, scf.for result/iter-arg, scf.if result) mapping the demand dim through reassociations and dropped dims; on the owning alloc, set or LCM-union the attrs; erase consumed marks; emitError for marks that would have to cross blocks or live on unranked memrefs
stages.where: PropagateAlignUtil.cpp:1934-1975 (pattern), 575-749 + 790-836 (per-op up cases), driven from EnableStrideAlign.cpp:759-763

stages.name: Seed AIV TCB marks from AIC (Ascend950 only)
stages.what: When the target is Ascend950 and any FixpipeOp exists, collect stride-align attrs from tightly-coupled-buffer marks in AIC functions and create matching per-dim marks on the AIV marks with the same TCB id, so cube-side padding demands reach the vector side

stages.name: Exchange demands to a fixed point (down → union → up)
stages.what: Repeat up to 10 rounds: copy demands down through users (cast/subview-dim-remap/collapse/expand/reshape/bitcast/scf.for init/scf.if yield; yield-skipped on regbase), union demands across the UB memref operands of every hivm structured op (LoadOp/StoreOp excluded as GM, CopyOp source excluded from back-propagation) after filtering already-satisfied demands, then push everything up to allocations again; stop when the alloc-level align-info map stops changing, otherwise emitError
stages.where: EnableStrideAlign.cpp:591-634 (loop), 563-589 (down+among drivers), PropagateAlignUtil.cpp:508-573 + 1977-1991 (down), EnableStrideAlign.cpp:216-304 + 469-481 (among), AdjustAlignUtil.cpp:47-135 + 509-600 (demand filtering)

stages.name: Strip consumed marks
stages.what: Remove the two stride-align attrs from every remaining annotation.mark op — the demands now live as attrs on allocations (or were dropped as already satisfied)

stages.name: Re-allocate padded buffers and rewire all users
stages.what: For each alloc-like op still carrying the attrs: compute per-dim alignment units (arch-dependent), build the aligned shape (pad dim grown + trailing 1), and if it differs, create the padded alloc, rescale buffer_size_in_byte marks by the static-volume ratio (ceil), insert a rank-reduced subview recovering the logical shape, push the new type through every user via unrealized casts (retyping views, loops, ifs, scopes, calls), and erase the old alloc; if shapes already match, just drop the attrs

stages.name: Repair failed propagation, then certify
stages.what: Replace uses tagged 'PropagateFailure' with fresh empty buffers + hivm.hir.copy, inserting dominator-ordered copies around writes on both sides; on regbase, materialize remaining static UB layout casts as alloc+copy; on membase only, stamp hivm.storage_aligned on the function; any earlier per-function failure aborts the walk and fails the pass

control_flow: The pass driver (runOnOperation) owns the order; each phase runs the greedy rewriter to exhaustion before the next phase starts
The fixed-point loop (stage 4) re-runs three pattern phases until the alloc-level demand map is stable, capped at 10 iterations, then the one-shot allocation rewrite (stage 6) happens once per alloc
Functions are walked sequentially, not in parallel, because the rewrite can reach into already-visited VF callees via propagateFuncCallOp
data_flow: Demands flow: mark on a leaf-ish value → (down) marks on users → (among) unioned marks across op operands → (up) attrs on the owning alloc; conflicts merge by LCM of byte values per dim
Shapes flow the opposite way at rewrite time: padded alloc type → strided subview type → retyped users; when a type cannot be pushed further, an explicit copy cuts the flow
Buffer byte-size annotations are rescaled at the moment a buffer grows, before users are re-pointed

implementation_view.aspect: Phases over one IR, not one pattern set
implementation_view.description: The pass applies different pattern families in a fixed sequence (normalize → up → fixed-point down/among/up → strip → alloc rewrite → repair) rather than one monolithic greedy set, because up-propagation consumes marks that down-propagation creates and vice versa

Demands travel as DenseI32ArrayAttr pairs (stride_align_dims / stride_align_value_in_byte) on annotation.mark ops and, once they reach memory, as the same attrs on alloc ops; this lets greedy patterns re-discover demands each round

Legality violations on the marks themselves (unranked, cross-block, mismatched attrs, non-convergence) fail the pass via emitError/signalPassFailure; layout changes that merely cannot be typed through a user are downgraded to explicit hivm.hir.copy materialization

conceptual_view.description: The pass owns no heuristic about who needs alignment — producers decide that. It only resolves demands into shapes, which is why it can run unconditionally: without marks it is a cheap no-op
The original logical memref shape always survives as the subview; only the physical allocation grows. Downstream code sees consistent strided types and can keep addressing the un-padded view

conceptual_view.aspect: Target fork is a shape-math detail
conceptual_view.description: membase and RegBase disagree only on which dim absorbs the padding (next dim vs the dim itself under a unit-stride last dim) and on whether a certification attribute is stamped; everything else in the machinery is shared

provenance.source: bishengir/test/Dialect/HIVM/hivm-enable-storage-align.mlir @HEAD 90037fe33, function test_elementwise_unary_op_unaligned — FileCheck expectations recorded in the repo; NOT executed in this analysis

canonical_example.initial_state: memref.alloc() : memref<2x15xf16, #hivm.address_space<ub>> with two identical marks {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: 0>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: 32>}, consumed by a bishengir_test.elementwise_unary; module has no hacc.target, so the target defaults to membase 910B
canonical_example.inputs: One static 2D UB buffer, one demand: dim-0 row stride must be a multiple of 32 bytes (f16 → 16 elements)
execution_trace: Normalize: both marks are already sorted — no change
Up-propagate: the demand leaves the marks and lands as {0, 32} attrs on the alloc
Fixed point: the elementwise op's UB operand set unions {0,32} onto the alloc; map stable → stop
Strip: mark ops lose the stride-align attrs

Alloc rewrite: collectAlignUnits yields unit 16 elements for the pad dim (membase: marked dim 0 pads dim 1); aligned shape [2,16,1] ≠ [2,15,1] → new memref.alloc() : memref<2x16x1xf16, ub> + memref.subview [0,0,0][2,15,1][1,1,1]; old alloc erased
canonical_example.result: CHECK expects memref<2x16x1xf16, ub> alloc plus subview, 'CHECK-NOT: annotation.mark', and hivm.storage_aligned on the function — the logical 2x15 view is unchanged, the physical rows are 16 elements apart

state_transitions.before: marks on leaf-ish values; allocs carry no align attrs
state_transitions.operation: fixed-point loop of down/union/up pattern phases (max 10 rounds), tracking the alloc-level align-info map between rounds
state_transitions.after: every surviving demand sits as attrs on an alloc; alloc map unchanged between rounds
state_transitions.reason: demands created downward (e.g. through scf.for inits) can unlock new upward unions; iteration is the only way to settle multi-op cycles

state_transitions.before: annotation.mark ops with stride-align attrs exist throughout the function
state_transitions.operation: normalize sorts them; up-propagation consumes them into alloc attrs; down/among create fresh ones; RemoveAlignMarkPattern strips survivors
state_transitions.after: no stride-align mark attrs remain on mark ops
state_transitions.reason: marks are transient currency; the alloc attrs are the durable form the rewrite consumes

state_transitions.before: memref.alloc with identity layout and un-padded dims (e.g. <2x15xf16, ub>)
state_transitions.operation: EnableAlignAllocation creates the padded alloc, rescales buffer_size_in_byte marks, inserts the logical subview, and replaceAndPropagateMemRefType retypes all users; un-propagatable users get the PropagateFailure tag first and are cut by copies afterwards
state_transitions.after: padded alloc (identity layout) + strided subview with the original logical shape; PropagateFailure tags resolved; on regbase remaining static UB casts materialized as alloc+copy
state_transitions.reason: the whole point of the pass: physical rows padded, logical shape preserved

state_transitions.operation: after all rewrites succeeded, the driver sets the unit attr on the func
state_transitions.after: function certified 'all operations aligned'; regbase functions are deliberately left unstamped
state_transitions.reason: master metadata contract gated to membase targets (commit a82e34730)

decisions.question: Which dimension absorbs the padding for a demand on dim d?
decisions.condition: target architecture (membase vs RegBase) and whether the last memref dim is unit-stride
outcomes: membase (or non-unit-stride last dim): pad dim d+1 — 'the stride is aligned by aligning the next dimension'
regbase with unit-stride last dim: pad dim d itself
decisions.reason: the two targets place the alignment requirement on different physical strides; collectAlignUnits encodes the fork and RegBase additionally requires the unit-stride last dim to take its branch

decisions.question: Rewrite the allocation or leave it alone?
decisions.condition: alignedShape (padded + trailing unit dim) vs the original shape
outcomes: different: new padded alloc + subview + full user rewiring + old alloc erased
equal: no rewrite; both attrs removed from the alloc ('no need to do alignment')
decisions.reason: already-aligned buffers must not grow a spurious trailing dim or pay rewrite cost; the test suite pins the no-subview outcome

decisions.question: Keep a demand during propagation or drop it?
decisions.condition: per-demand check when a mark is moved onto a new value: GM memory space, all-1 dims before the align dim, an already-satisfying existing stride, ops that will lower to scalar loops, Load/Store with implicit-transpose last axis
outcomes: drop (adjustAlignDim → nullopt): demand considered already satisfied or irrelevant
keep (possibly remapped dim, LCM-merged with an existing demand on the same dim)
decisions.reason: over-padding wastes UB and can break collapse legality; the filter runs at every propagation hop

decisions.question: Retype a user or cut it with a copy?
decisions.condition: can the aligned type be pushed through the user (view ops, loops, ifs, scopes, calls — with their guards) or does propagation fail?
outcomes: retype: cast pushed down, loop/if/scope/call signatures updated
cut: user tagged PropagateFailure; handlePropagateFailure later inserts empty+copy and dominator-ordered sync copies
decisions.reason: typing through is free at runtime; copying costs bandwidth but is always legal — the pass prefers free and falls back only when forced

decisions.question: Stamp the certification attribute?
outcomes: membase: set hivm.storage_aligned on each device func
regbase: never stamp (comment: regbase (A5) targets must not carry this attribute)
decisions.reason: the attr is a membase-only master metadata contract; stamping was explicitly gated to membase in commit a82e34730 and the regbase median-kernel test asserts absence

decisions.question: Propagate cube-side demands to the vector side?
decisions.condition: target is Ascend950 AND a FixpipeOp exists in the module (isMarkStrideForAiv)
outcomes: yes: copy stride-align info from AIC TCB marks onto AIV marks with the same TCB id (skipping hivm.vector_function funcs and allocs already marked)
no: AIV side keeps only its own demands
decisions.reason: shared tightly-coupled buffers must satisfy the stricter union of cube and vector requirements; the trigger is deliberately narrow (950 + fixpipe present)

contracts.form: annotation.mark {hivm.stride_align_dims, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte} on ranked UB memref values; byte value = hardware align bytes of the memory space; missing/mismatched attrs are a pass failure, not a skip

contracts.consumer: the marking side of the pair (upstream of this pass)
contracts.element: skip-stride-align protection for VF vload roots
contracts.form: regbase-only marks on load roots flowing to vload in VFs; EnableStrideAlign consumes no such marks itself — it only ever sees the demands that survived the marking side
padded memref.alloc types behind strided memref.subview results; arith-computed dynamic pad sizes; rescaled buffer_size_in_byte marks

contracts.consumer: membase metadata consumers (location not determined inside this repository)
contracts.form: UnitAttr on each rewritten device func, membase targets only; declared semantics: 'all of the operations in this function are aligned'

constraints.statement: The align byte value must be a whole number of elements: collectAlignUnits asserts alignBits % elementBitWidth == 0, and demands smaller than the element size are skipped as trivially satisfied
Marks must live on ranked memrefs inside one block: unranked memrefs and demands that would cross blocks (except scf.for iter args) are emitErrors that fail the pass

The demand exchange must converge within 10 fixed-point rounds (and each greedy round within 10000 iterations), otherwise the pass emits 'propagate storage align failure and match the max iterations' and fails
RegBase keeps the last memref dim unit-stride: the regbase branch of collectAlignUnits only engages when isLastMemrefDimUnitStride, and regbase skips scf.yield type propagation entirely
The pass requires ModuleOp scope and a sequential function walk: aligned allocs propagate through func.call into VF callees, so FuncOp-parallel nesting could race on already-visited functions
buffer_size_in_byte annotations must be rescaled whenever a buffer grows, using ceil division of the static-volume ratio so the buffer is never under-allocated
memref.view is never aligned ('it assumes empty layout'); GM operands and tensor IR are out of scope by design

invariants.statement: The logical memref shape is preserved: users always see the original shape, either directly (already aligned) or through a strided subview of the padded allocation
After a successful run no stride-align mark attrs remain in the rewritten function: they are consumed into alloc attrs and finally stripped (marks) or removed/erased with their alloc (attrs)

Row strides of marked dimensions are multiples of the demanded byte count after the rewrite (e.g. 15 f16 elements → stride 16; 7 f16 → stride 16; 4 f32 → stride 8), while unmarked dims keep their natural layout
Conflicting demands on the same buffer merge by LCM of byte values per dim — the union is always at least as strict as each input demand

assumptions.statement: Demands arriving without the gating marking passes (e.g. hand-written marks in tests, or marks from custom producers) are honored identically — the pass reads attrs, not provenance
Downstream consumers of hivm.storage_aligned exist outside the analyzed repository; within it the attr is written but never read

boundaries.statement: Static and dynamic shapes (dynamic pad dims get arith ceil-align sequences), view ops, scf.for/scf.if, scope.scope results, and func.call into outlined VF callees are all propagated, each backed by a dedicated test
scf.while is explicitly not handled in the yield propagation path ('TODO: need to support whileOp better in strideAlign case'); non-identity-layout collapse borrowing is gated on contiguity

GM loads/stores are never stride-aligned ('no need to do stride align for gm'), a CopyOp's source is excluded from back-propagation, memref.view is never aligned, and regbase targets must not carry hivm.storage_aligned
Marks that would have to cross blocks (outside scf.for iter args) or live on unranked memrefs fail the pass outright rather than being ignored
The rewrite can grow buffers (padding ratio) and introduce explicit copies when typing fails; a pathological demand graph costs up to 10 fixed-point rounds of greedy rewriting before failing
Who reads hivm.storage_aligned downstream: no reader was found in bishengir/lib at HEAD; the consumer may live in out-of-repo lowering or tooling, and this analysis did not determine it

placement.why_here: It needs finished memref IR (post-bufferization), the marks that only exist after the gated marking passes, and FoldAllocReshape already applied — and everything after it in hivmPostBufferizationOptimizationPipeline (AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT decompose, InferHIVMDataLayout/nd2nz, buffer-size constantization) is specified against the final, aligned strides, so it must run at the end of alignStoragePipeline
placement.why_not_earlier: Before bufferization the buffers are tensors and the demand marks do not exist yet; before FoldAllocReshape there are more reshape/view ops between a mark and its allocation, each one a chance for reassociation-based demand mapping to fail
placement.why_not_later: Every later consumer (data-layout inference, nd2nz conversion, buffer-size constantization, memory planning/lowering) reads shapes and strides to make allocation decisions; changing them after those passes would invalidate their results, and the pass itself wants to be the last writer of buffer shapes
placement.status: placement derived from pipeline order and pass dependencies read at HEAD; the not-earlier/not-later rationale is inference from that order

ownership.component: bishengir/lib/Dialect/HIVM/Transforms/AlignBuffer/ (EnableStrideAlign.cpp plus shared helpers PropagateAlignUtil.cpp, AdjustAlignUtil.cpp, Util.h)
ownership.notes: The pass shares its helper library with the producer passes in the same directory, so mark-format changes are joint changes across the directory

complexity.size: EnableStrideAlign.cpp 813 lines; PropagateAlignUtil.cpp 1992; AdjustAlignUtil.cpp 610; AlignBuffer/Util.h 167 — roughly 3.6k lines of pass+helpers
complexity.structure: 7 sequential phases, ~10 pattern families plus 2 alloc template instantiations, one 10-round fixed point with 10000-iteration greedy caps
complexity.provenance: measured (wc/read at HEAD) for sizes; derived for phase/pattern counts

key_takeaways: Mark/enable split: cheap producers annotate which row strides must be hardware-aligned; EnableStrideAlign is the single consumer that turns marks into padded allocations, merging conflicting demands with LCM union semantics.

The pad dimension is arch-dependent: membase pads the dim after the marked one; RegBase (A5, unit-stride last dim) pads the marked dim itself. Either way the logical shape survives unchanged behind a strided subview.

It runs unconditionally at the end of alignStoragePipeline — only the two marking passes are gated by enable-hivm-auto-storage-align — because with no marks present it is a cheap no-op that leaves allocs untouched.

It is the last writer of buffer shapes in the post-bufferization pipeline: everything after it (decompose, nd2nz data-layout inference, buffer-size constantization) consumes the final padded shapes and strided layouts.
Failures are loud or compensated, never silent: unranked/cross-block marks and non-convergence fail the pass, while un-propagatable layout changes are cut with explicit hivm.hir.copy fallbacks.

pass.operation_scope: ModuleOp (Pass<"hivm-enable-stride-align", "ModuleOp">): the description states ModuleOp scope is required so FuncOp-parallel nesting cannot race when aligned allocs propagate through func.call into VF callees; runOnOperation walks non-host func::FuncOps sequentially and signals pass failure if any function fails

pipeline_placements.order: AlignAllocSize → [if enable-hivm-auto-storage-align: PreMarkStrideAlign → MarkStrideAlign] → memref FoldAllocReshape → EnableStrideAlign (module-level, ungated, last)

called at 560 after HIVMAggregatedDecomposeOp(AFTER_RECOGNIZE_BROADCAST) and before HIVMAggregatedDecomposeOp(AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT), the canonicalizer, InferHIVMDataLayout and the buffer-size passes
bufferizationPipeline → SubBlockGuardCleanup → hivmPostBufferizationOptimizationPipeline (which contains this pass) → force-inline scopes → InjectIR

ir_contract.input: Post-bufferization memref IR with transient demand marks: annotation.mark {hivm.stride_align_dims = array<i32: d...>, hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte = array<i32: b...>} on ranked UB memref values, plus the same attrs possibly already on alloc-like ops from earlier rounds; marks may sit on alloc results, view results, scf.for iter-args/results, scf.if results
ir_contract.realized_alignment: For each demand not already satisfied: the owning allocation is re-created with the pad dim grown to lcm(alignBits/elemBits) elements (dim d+1 on membase, dim d on regbase with unit-stride last dim; trailing 1 dim appended when needed) and a rank-reduced strided subview hands every user the original logical shape — e.g. memref<2x15xf16,ub> → alloc memref<2x16x1xf16,ub> + subview strided<[16,1]>; memref<5x8x7xf16,ub> (regbase, mark dim 2) → callee arg type memref<5x8x7xf16, strided<[128,16,1]>,ub>
ir_contract.metadata: buffer_size_in_byte marks rescaled by ceil(static-volume ratio); stride-align marks/attrs fully consumed; membase-only hivm.storage_aligned UnitAttr stamped on device functions
ir_contract.consumers: AFTER_HIVM_STRIDE_ALIGNMENT decompose, InferHIVMDataLayout (copy→nd2nz), AutoInferBufferSize/ConstantizeBufferSize, and any later lowering reading shapes/strides

consumed: annotation.mark ops with hivm.stride_align_dims / hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte (removed after normalization+propagation)
same attrs on memref.alloc/memref.alloca ops (consumed or removed by the alloc rewrite)
created: hivm.stride_align_dims / hivm.stride_align_value_in_byte (transient, on values and allocs during propagation)
PropagateFailure tag attr (transient, on un-propagatable casts/users)
hivm.storage_aligned UnitAttr (persistent, device funcs, membase only)

legality.summary: The pass does not pattern-refuse silently: demands that cannot legally propagate are compile errors, demands that are already satisfied are dropped, and layouts that cannot be typed through a user are compensated with copies
hard_failures: mark attrs missing or size-mismatched ('align info must contain align dims and align bytes')
align bits not a multiple of the element bit width (assert)
mark on unranked memref; mark crossing blocks outside scf.for iter args
demand unmappable through a collapse/expand reassociation ('cannot align <dim> axis')
demand exchange not converged in 10 rounds
soft_outcomes: already-satisfied demands dropped (GM space, all-1 prefix dims, existing stride already aligned, scalar-loop lowering, implicit-transpose load/store)
un-propagatable users cut by empty+copy with dominator-ordered sync copies
already-aligned allocs left byte-for-byte unchanged (attrs removed, no subview)

rewrite.style: Multi-phase greedy pattern application per function plus direct rewriter mutations in the driver; the alloc rewrite is a template over AllocLikeOp instantiated for memref.alloc and memref.alloca
pattern_families: PropagateAlignAmongOperationOperands<all HIVM vector ops + CopyOp> (operand union)
rewrite.non_local_effects: propagateFuncCallOp retypes callee signatures and entry-block arg types of outlined VF callees; scf.for init/iter-arg/result and scope results are retyped with boundary casts
